title: Keep Going
author: Simtetik
selftext:
As a fellow dev using AI to help build the game of my dreams, i just want to say: keep going.

The "AI slop" crowd wants you to stop. They think they are protecting art and human creativity. But what they are actually protecting is capitalism's cage. Most of us in this sub dreamed of spending our days building games. Being creative. Having fun. But capitalism demands we become a cog in the machine. It restricts our time so our creativity is restricted to mere hours per week. And it's the hours when our energy is most depleted.

Pre generative AI, a lot of us tried to use whatever spare energy and time we had to get our visions into reality. But damn it's hard. At every step you find there are some other obscure bits of knowledge or skill you're missing that now require many hours to master. To some that is the beauty in the making. But really, a lot of it is just thick mud you had to wade through in order to get to the vision. 

Now we can bypass the mud. We can focus on the vision. Finally it is actually about human creativity and not about the mud. If you are doing this for the passion of games, keep going.

The barrier to entry was never high, that's just an excuse people use to delude themselves.

Before AI it had never been easier to make a game. There's YouTube and the internet with hundreds of thousands of completely free learning materials along with lots of cheap and completely free game dev tools and engines.

replies.author: Good-Acanthaceae-136
replies.body:
I work freelance, mostly web and 3D work but it's drying up for obvious reasons. My project is more an experience rather than a game with a linear story and gameplay loops. I do use AI but only for the occasional help with code, mainly shader code because that's my weakest area.

This is all irrelevant to my point anyway. The only barrier to making something is yourself. People made games long before AI and they weren't all rich kids or people that didn't have to work or had no family etc. They just had drive, passion and dedication.

People saying they couldn't make a game without AI are basically just saying they didn't want to give the time to learning and creating it.

replies.author: cheyumaama
replies.body: Are you telling me it's easy to learn 3D modeling and animations? I tried setting up a scene in Blender before AI with my own handcrafted 3D assets and it was impossibly hard and extremely time consuming for a beginner

replies.author: Good-Acanthaceae-136
replies.body:
Yes it's easy, it just takes some determination and dedication. Spend a couple of weeks learning Blender for example and you will be good enough to start making models.  I'm not saying you will be an expert, that comes with time and experience but you should tailor your game project around your skillset.

Too many people here are looking to have AI do the skilled part for them because they are too lazy to learn. AI should be a tool to enhance your skills not do the skilled work for you.

replies.body: Why would anybody do that? This is like some fool during the industrial revolution saying "You need to still put the chips in the bag or put the wrappers around the chocolates. The machines should only enhance your work, it should not do it entirely."

Yeah, getting real tired of the anti-ai crowd.

I've been a programmer for over 15 years now and use AI. Even hand crafting things is getting me called "No effort, AI vibe coding slop". People are completely deranged and delusional. The funniest thing is when you look at the work most of these anti-ai crowd they are most of the time unskilled, uncreative losers. So many of them. I don't really understand why they wouldn't want to use something so empowering.

I've been completely bashed for my AI use and mass downvoted/negative reviewed on a few games, sent awful messages and DMs, then you go look at that persons profile and it's just the most dogshit uncreative "hand crafted" slop I've ever seen. Most of the time these people are learning to code or something and they can't even make the main menu of a game or do basic UI work. Just stupid.

This all reminds me of the early 2000s, when iphones and android was getting popular. People had the exact same reaction to early phones and wifi, just so stupid. In the end AI will win, it will probably make us all obsolete too, but until then we can have some fun with this incredible technology.

I love looking at other peoples work too, and even though I've spent most of my life studying software engineering it is awesome to see how we're finally at the stage that motivated me to get in the industry in the first place.

But yeah, I want to rant a bit too. Fuck these loser ass anti AI people, jesus christ they're awful and think they are the gatekeepers of "good games" when they can't even name a single "real artist" or "good game". Their favorite most creative game ever made was some dogshit minecraft mod that barely functions and is incomplete.

comments.author: dmarshallgaming
comments.body:
This hits home. I'm a solo dev with a day job, and the honest truth is my game wouldn't exist without AI. I'd have run out of evenings long before I ran out of ideas.

The planets in my game are AI-generated, and I say so openly on the store page. The ships, effects and UI are licensed packs and the audio is licensed too. The part AI saved me from wasn't the creative part. It was exactly the mud you describe: the hundred small things between "I know what this should feel like" and it actually running.

What I'd add for anyone reading: keep going, but also keep playtesting with real people. AI got me to a working game fast, but every big improvement came from watching someone else play it and struggle in places I never expected. The vision is still yours to check.

Be upfront about what you used, too. The people who are going to hate it will hate it either way, and everyone else respects honesty.

comments.author: OkVariety8064
comments.body:
The devil is in the details. Depends what you mean by making a game. If you literally mean just finishing a project to the degree that it is a functional game, and enjoying it by yourself or with your family, then certainly this is a great step forward.

But if you mean it in the sense that your game, specifically, would find an audience, and maybe even make some money, I think it's too early to tell. In any case what you have to understand is that this AI is not some sort of secret. If you can use it, so can everyone else. And there is a lot of pent up energy for making games. Whether there is similar energy for sifting through ever greater numbers of published games remains to be seen.

But I doubt that. Gaming is already a saturated market. Most games make next to nothing. The saturation will only get worse. Still, even now there are different gaming markets. An indie quality game on Steam still has it easier than a similar one on mobile, even if both ecosystems are very saturated. The markets keep evolving and it's not easy to see what extreme increase in production will mean.

Some people say that this is just a temporary deluge, and most people will see that their games won't find an audience, leave, and only the dedicated authors will remain. But if we look at books, music or social media, the chances of success being astronomically small doesn't really deter ever more people from trying. I don't think this explosion of content is going to be temporary, but rather that gaming will start to look like YouTube or TikTok. When the product itself (video or game) becomes simple enough to make, to stand out you need something else: Marketing, your own story, or connections. Money will still make all that easier.
